The paper was published in the Journal of Electromagnetic Waves and Applications, Vol. 24, 51-60, 2010
All authors are from the National Laboratory of Antennas and Microwave Technology at Xidian University, Xi'an, China
The reference antenna consists of a rectangle (24mm × 12mm) and a circular base with 12mm radius
The substrate used is FR-4 with relative dielectric constant of 4.4 and thickness of 0.8mm
The coplanar waveguide feed has length of 10mm and width of 0.8mm
The gap width between feed line and ground patch is 0.2mm
Surface current distribution was analyzed at three specific frequencies: 3 GHz, 8 GHz, and 10 GHz
The modified antenna uses circular and semicircular holes to reduce metallic patch area
VSWR comparison shows the impedance characteristics of both antennas are almost identical
Radiation patterns were compared in E-plane and H-plane (x-y and y-z planes)
The frequency range analyzed spans from 2 GHz to 20 GHz
RCS measurements were performed for both open-circuit and short-circuit load conditions
The modified antenna achieves lower RCS than the reference antenna across the entire frequency band
In high frequency ranges, RCS reduction is greater due to smaller geometrical size of the modified antenna
In low frequency ranges, antenna structural mode scattering behaves as low frequency resonance scattering
The proposed technique does not change the surface current distribution patterns of the antenna
Measured and simulated VSWR results show good agreement for the modified antenna
The gain curves of both antennas are nearly identical across the frequency band
The technique is applicable to printed antennas with UWB requirements
The research was supported by the National Natural Science Fund of P.R. China (No. 60801042)
The modified antenna was successfully fabricated and experimentally verified
Structural mode RCS can be calculated from the difference between open-circuit and short-circuit RCS values
The incident wave direction parallel to the z-axis represents the most threatening direction for RCS evaluation
The proposed technique represents an effective approach for RCS control in printed antenna design
